content.title: Community Survey
content.summary: The 2025 Community Survey in Arvada, which closed on October 31, 2025, allows residents to evaluate their satisfaction with quality of life, community amenities, and local government. The survey serves as a feedback tool for the City government, helping to identify areas of success and concern while guiding community planning and resource allocation. Results from the survey indicate varying levels of satisfaction and perceptions of the city's direction over the years.
content.body:
## The 2025 Community Survey

**The 2025 Community Survey closed on Oct. 31, 2025.**

Since 1997, Arvada residents have been rating their satisfaction with regard to quality of life, community amenities, and local government via the Community Survey. The survey functions as a consumer report card by providing residents the opportunity to rate their satisfaction with their quality of life, community amenities, and local government.

### Access the 2025 results

[City of Arvada Community Survey 2025 Results Probolsky Research (PDF)](/DocumentCenter/View/7289/City-of-Arvada-Community-Survey-2025-Results-Probolsky-Research-PDF)

Take a deep dive into the results on the [interactive Arvada Community Survey dashboard](https://urldefense.com/v3/__https://lookerstudio.google.com/u/0/reporting/963bd2ae-74f3-4953-889d-0bb6f8114789/page/p_prz2hmjq1d__;!!ErRPcXOCvh0!_sc4ey8-lALJ34dvWMZK4qw_DNsiQ9hrihNgn-NbOEKQszOScVvWCZALsfxrHye2AbyLFI6g5W3W42pTRVQwxQ$)

## How is the survey used?

The survey gives residents an opportunity to provide feedback to the City government on what they believe is working well and what is not, and to communicate their priorities regarding community planning and resource allocation. The survey invites your opinions about how the City uses tax dollars, how safe you feel in the City and your neighborhood, and how you perceive Arvada as a place to live, among a number of other areas of interest. This information is critical to the City's understanding of the current and future needs of Arvada residents, like you.

## 2025 respondents by district

![Respondents by district. 23.3% (1), 22.8% (2), 23.3% (3), 22.5% (4), 8.1% (refused)  ](/ImageRepository/Document?documentId=7222)

## How can 1200 people represent all of Arvada?

How can 1200 residents represent the views of 124,000 people? Public opinion researchers use a statistical method called sampling, which allows us to draw conclusions about an entire community by surveying a smaller, carefully selected group.

Think of it like tasting a spoonful of soup—you don’t need to eat the whole pot to know if it’s well-seasoned. Similarly, a well-designed survey sample reflects the views of the broader population.

To ensure accuracy, researchers:

- Determine the minimum sample size using a standard mathematical formula.
- Match survey demographics to U.S. Census data, ensuring fair representation by age, gender, ethnicity and geography.

All surveys come with a margin of error and a confidence level:

- 95% confidence level: If we conducted this survey 100 times, 95 times the results would be nearly the same.
- ±3% margin of error: If 60% of respondents agree on an issue, the true percentage in the full population is likely between 57% and 63%.

The City works with an independent research firm to ensure the Community Survey follows the highest industry standards.
